info.title: OddsLink API
info.summary: Live odds and prices from every book we cover, in one JSON API.
info.description:
Fixtures and prices from every sportsbook, exchange and prediction market we cover, joined
onto one fixture and returned in one JSON response. Every book is available on every plan,
and there is no regional gating.

## Response format

Fixture and price fields use plain, familiar names: `bookmakers[] -> markets[] ->
outcomes[{name, price, point}]`, with `home_team` / `away_team` on the fixture. A few
things worth knowing about how our format works:

- The API key is sent in the `X-API-Key` request header only. There is no query parameter
  alternative, since a key in a URL can end up recorded by a proxy or a log.
- A market's `key` is its family (`h2h`, `h2h_3_way`, `spreads`, `totals`, `team_totals`, ...). A
  period market also carries `period` (`1h`, `2h`, `1q`..`4q`, `1p`..`3p`, `f5`), so the
  first-half total is `{"key": "totals", "period": "1h"}`. A full-game market has no
  `period` field at all. Ask for periods with the `periods` parameter: omit it for the full
  game only, `periods=1h,1q` for just those periods, `periods=full,1h` for the full game
  plus the first half, `periods=all` for everything.
- `price` is one number. Under the default `oddsFormat=american` it is always an integer
  (`-110`, `124`); under `oddsFormat=decimal` it is a decimal number above 1 (`1.91`).
  `point` is a decimal number (`2.5`, `-3.0`) and is absent on a moneyline.
  Historical exchange quotes instead carry `bid_prob`, `ask_prob`, and `mid_prob`,
  with `price: null` in either odds format; an absent probability stays null.
- `last_update` is present on every price and can be `null`. A `null` value means we do
  not yet measure a fetch time for that book, and it is never an estimate. A price older
  than its book's normal update rhythm is removed rather than shown as stale.
- `size` is a typed object: `kind` (`posted_limit` or `resting_depth`; `contracts` is reserved) and
  `amount`. It is present on every outcome the book states a limit or depth for: the main
  line, each alternate line, period markets and team totals alike. It is absent, never
  zero, where the book states none for that exact line.
- `unmatched_bookmakers` is a sorted list of book keys. With `bookmakers=`, it
  accounts for each requested book with no rows in the selected markets. Without that
  filter, game odds account for all catalogue books; props account for all props-capable
  catalogue books. This reports absence, not its cause or an outage. The
  catalogue's `has_player_props` says an integration exists somewhere, not in every sport.
- `id` is a stable, canonical id built from the sport, the two teams' canonical names in
  alphabetical order and a UTC kickoff date assigned to the fixture, for example
  `nfl:atlantafalcons-carolinapanthers:2026-09-20`. The order is alphabetical, not
  away-then-home: read `home_team` and `away_team` for that. When one pair meets twice
  on one date (a baseball doubleheader) the later game carries a `:g2` suffix. The id does
  not change when a bookmaker spells a team differently. A retained id can carry an earlier
  kickoff date after the scheduled kickoff changes. Read `commence_time` for the current
  scheduled kickoff, rather than deriving it from the id. Treat the id as an opaque string.
- Props have their own endpoints. Each row covers one player, stat and line per book, with
  every outcome for that line together in one place.
- History has its own endpoints: openers, closing lines and the full recorded series.
- Errors are nested under `error`: `code`, `message`, `docs_url`, `request_id`.

## Compression

Send `Accept-Encoding: gzip` on every call. Odds responses are large and highly
repetitive, so gzip cuts a typical multi-market response from about 2.6 MB to about
0.29 MB. Most HTTP clients send the header and decompress for you; `curl` needs
`--compressed` and PHP's curl needs `CURLOPT_ENCODING`.

## What counts as a request

Only calls that return prices count against your monthly allowance: the odds endpoints,
the props endpoints and the history endpoints. Listing sports, bookmakers, markets and
fixtures is free on every plan, and the account endpoints are free too. All of them still
follow your plan's speed limit. Each operation below states whether it counts
(`x-counts-as-request`). A free call never answers `ALLOWANCE_SPENT`: once the month's
allowance is used up, the free calls keep working.

## Live feed (WebSocket)

Prices pushed to you as they change, instead of you asking for them. Sold under the name
"WebSocket": an add-on (+$99/month) on Growth and Scale, included on Business and Enterprise,
refused with `403 PLAN_REQUIRED` on Free and Starter, using the same envelope shape a REST
refusal uses, returned as the WebSocket handshake's own HTTP response before the connection is
accepted. Not metered as a request. Full details (every message type, the resume protocol and
the close codes) are under the `x-websocket-feed` key of this document (most tooling that
renders this file skips unrecognised top-level keys; read the raw YAML/JSON for them, or see
`oddslink.app/docs`).

In short: connect to `wss://oddslink.app/v1/feed` with the same `X-API-Key` header REST uses.
Send `{"type": "subscribe", "sport": "...", ...}` (the same filters as `GET /v1/sports/
{sport}/odds`: `league`, `tournament`, `bookmakers`, `markets`, `event_ids`) and you get a full
Picture, the same row shape this document describes for that endpoint, followed by `changes`
messages grouped at most once a second, each carrying a `cursor`. A price going stale or a book
delisting it arrives as an explicit `removal`; silence never means removal. Reconnect with
`{"type": "resume", "token": "<last cursor's token>"}` to replay what you missed if you were
gone under about a minute; otherwise you get `picture_required` and send a fresh `subscribe`. A
server `heartbeat` arrives every 5 seconds.

## Breaking changes

Within one version, changes only add: new endpoints, new optional parameters, new response
fields, new values you should be ready to see. We do not rename or remove a field, change a
field's type, or change what an existing parameter does by default. A change that cannot be
made that way ships as a new version, with the previous one kept running through a notice
period.

A response field whose value comes from a documented list (a book's `kind`, a `size`'s
`kind`, a plan name) can gain a new value within a version. Those lists are marked
`x-extensible-enum` instead of `enum`, so a client generated from this file reads them as
plain strings; handle a value you do not recognise instead of failing on it.

get.summary: List sports
get.description: Every sport key we cover, each with an `active` flag. `soccer` and `tennis` are aggregate keys: pass `league=epl` or `tournament=atp_hangzhou` to narrow them, or omit the selector to receive all currently available competitions in one response. The older per-competition keys (`epl`, `la_liga`, `tennis_atp_hangzhou`, ...) remain listed and callable as aliases. League keys are listed whether in season or not. Tennis tournament aliases change every week, with their tour in the key (`tennis_atp_hangzhou`, `tennis_wta_seoul`, `tennis_challenger_genoa`, `tennis_itf_women_berkeley`, `tennis_utr_men_norfolk`, `tennis_billie_jean_king_cup`), and a doubles draw has its own key ending in `_doubles`. Tournaments change every week, so only the tennis tournaments we currently carry fixtures for are listed.

sports.summary: A handful of the sports we carry

get.summary: List bookmakers
get.description: Every book we cover: its key, its display title, its kind (sportsbook, exchange or prediction market), the sports it has been seen pricing, whether it has a player-props integration, and what a `size` from it means. A retired book, or one we no longer serve, does not appear here.

bookmakers.summary: A sportsbook and a prediction market

get.summary: List markets
get.description: Every market we serve, one entry per market key and period, with the sports it applies to and a short description. An entry with no `period` is the full-game market; baseball's only period is `f5` (first 5 innings) and there are no F3 or F7 markets. Pass `key` to `markets` and `period` to `periods`. `kind` says which endpoint takes the key: `game_line` keys go to `/v1/sports/{sport}/odds`, `player_prop` keys to `/v1/sports/{sport}/props`, where `markets` is required.

markets.summary: A full-game market, a first-5-innings one, and a player prop

value.description: Two-way match winner; soccer includes the draw.
Combined score, over or under a line (total games in tennis).

get.summary: List a sport's fixtures, no prices
get.description: Only fixtures that have not started, for every plan, with no bookmakers attached. Includes listed fixtures with no prices for the default odds markets. There is no date cap on aggregate soccer or tennis lists. Use `/events/live` for fixtures in play now; it needs in-play odds (Growth and up), NOT the live feed add-on.

get.summary: List fixtures in play, no prices
get.description: `/live` = fixtures in play now: started and not finished, using public `is_live`. Needs in-play odds (Growth and up), NOT the live feed add-on. The same selectors and formats as the upcoming list apply.

get.summary: List a sport's fixtures with prices
get.description: Only fixtures that have not started, for every plan, each with every book's price for the requested markets. A fixture is included only when at least one bookmaker remains after the requested bookmaker, market and period filters and price availability checks. Use `/events` to discover listed fixtures without prices. Aggregate soccer and tennis lists have no date cap. Use `/odds/live` for fixtures in play now; it needs in-play odds (Growth and up), NOT the live feed add-on. `soccer` and `tennis` return every currently available competition when their optional `league` / `tournament` selector is omitted; these larger responses may take longer. When `markets` is omitted, each available book returns its main `h2h`, `spreads` and `totals` markets. Requesting `spreads` or `totals` includes that market's complete main-first line ladder under one market object. Period markets (`periods=1h`, `periods=f5`, ...) and derivative markets (`team_totals`, ...) are refreshed on the book's own slower cadence and may be up to 15 minutes old; read each market's `last_update`. This is the call that counts against your allowance: one request regardless of how many fixtures or books come back.

american_iso.summary: Default format: American odds, ISO-8601 times

get.summary: List fixtures in play with prices
get.description: `/live` = fixtures in play now: started and not finished, using public `is_live`. Needs in-play odds (Growth and up), NOT the live feed add-on. The same selectors and formats as the upcoming list apply.

get.summary: One fixture's prices, including periods and full-game ladders
get.description: The same shape as `listOdds` for exactly one fixture. When `markets` is omitted, it returns the available main full-game `h2h`, `spreads` and `totals` markets. Add `periods` for period markets (`markets=spreads&periods=1h`); requesting full-game `spreads` or `totals` returns its complete main-first ladder under that key. Team totals use `team_totals`, where each outcome's `description` names the team. Period and derivative markets are refreshed on the book's own slower cadence and may be up to 15 minutes old; read each market's `last_update`. A plan without in-play odds (below Growth) asking for a fixture that has already started gets `403 PLAN_REQUIRED` naming `growth` as `required_plan`, the same shape props and history use, rather than that fixture's prices.

periods_and_ladders.summary: markets=h2h,spreads,team_totals&periods=full,1h: a first-half moneyline, a spread ladder and team totals

get.summary: Board sports with fixture counts
get.description: Every sport the public board offers, with how many fixtures it holds right now and how many are in play, busiest first. No API key. Cached a few seconds; per-address rate limited.

get.summary: The public board for one sport
get.description: Every fixture in the sport's board window (started up to 4 h ago, or starting within 36 h), each with every book's main h2h, spread and total. In play first. No API key; cached a few seconds; per-address rate limited; capped at 60 fixtures.

503.description: The board could not be read right now; retry shortly.

error.message: odds data could not be read right now; retry shortly

get.summary: The homepage's featured games
get.description: Up to three cards for the homepage: the busiest sports right now (fixtures times books), each with its next big upcoming game (never one in play), moneyline only, five books a card with the best price per side flagged. `cards` is empty when nothing qualifies. No API key; cached a few seconds; per-address rate limited.

get.summary: Player props across a sport's fixtures
get.description: Player props only for fixtures that have not started. Requires the Growth plan or above. Aggregate soccer and tennis lists have no date cap. Use `/props/live` for fixtures in play now; it needs in-play odds (Growth and up), NOT the live feed add-on. Each row covers one `(player, stat, line)` per book, with every outcome for that line (an over and an under, or a single side for a binary prop) together in one place. `stat` uses familiar market-key names such as `player_pass_yds` and `batter_hits`.

props.summary: One fixture's anytime-TD and passing-yards props

get.summary: Player props for fixtures in play
get.description: `/live` = fixtures in play now: started and not finished, using public `is_live`. Needs in-play odds (Growth and up), NOT the live feed add-on. The same selectors and formats as the upcoming list apply.

get.summary: Player props for one fixture
get.description: The same row shape as `listProps`, scoped to exactly one fixture. Growth plan and up.

get.summary: Discover archived fixture IDs
get.description: Discover stored fixture metadata. Empty duplicate kickoffs are excluded when another stored kickoff has recorded prices; entirely empty tracked fixtures remain discoverable. Scale covers stored kickoffs in the last 2 years; Business covers all archives. Date bounds are inclusive stored schedule times, not verified actual kickoff or finish times. If any eligible anchor matches the bounds, the fixture includes every eligible stored choice. Sorted by earliest eligible stored anchor then ID; this ordering never chooses the true kickoff. Continue with next_cursor using the same sport/date filters. Conflicting choices have commence_time null and history_ambiguous true. Use one stored_commence_times value as storedCommenceTime on a price route. Stored kickoffs within 30 minutes of each other are treated as one (earliest wins). Soccer fixtures carry `league: {key, title}` and tennis fixtures `tournament`, like current fixtures (`null` when the archive recorded none); the price and prop history bodies carry it too. Other sports carry neither.

parameters.name: commenceTimeFrom
parameters.description: Inclusive earliest stored kickoff, ISO with timezone or Unix seconds.

parameters.name: commenceTimeTo
parameters.description: Inclusive latest stored kickoff, ISO with timezone or Unix seconds.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque next_cursor from the preceding page with the same filters.

200.description: Stored fixture metadata; archive presence does not prove completion.

get.summary: The full recorded price series for one fixture
get.description: Recorded price history for one fixture. Where change rows exist, the first point per bookmaker and market contains the full market; later points contain only outcomes whose price, point or size changed, with their own values. Apply points in order to rebuild the market. A since-bounded window starts with a full market seeded from earlier changes. Fixtures without change rows retain whole-market checkpoint points. Exchange/prediction-market books retain whole-market checkpoint points even alongside sportsbook change rows. Their outcomes carry bid/ask/mid probabilities and a null price, with no inferred main line or opening checkpoint. Requires the Scale plan or above. History covers fixtures that have already finished, so an upcoming fixture is not found here: read its current prices from `/v1/sports/{sport}/odds` instead. Scale covers fixtures that started in the last 2 years; Business covers everything recorded. On Scale, a fixture that started more than 2 years ago is refused with `403 PLAN_REQUIRED` naming `business` as `required_plan`, never answered with a partial or empty series. The archive begins at `archive_from`, so a fixture from before that has nothing recorded, and this endpoint says so explicitly with `movement: not_recorded` rather than an empty array. The `movement` label describes recorded timestamp groups: one is `no_movement`, more than one is `recorded`. It does not prove that a price never changed between checkpoints.

200.description: The recorded series for this fixture.

series.summary: A spread that moved twice, a total recorded once

get.summary: Each book's opening line for one fixture
get.description: The outcomes captured when each book's market was first recorded on this fixture. Selections added later are not part of that opening checkpoint. Requires the Scale plan or above, with the same 2-years-or-everything split as the series endpoint (an older fixture on Scale is a `403 PLAN_REQUIRED` naming `business`). A market with nothing recorded is returned with `status: not_recorded` rather than left out of the list.

openers.summary: One recorded market, one never captured

get.summary: Each book's closing line for one fixture
get.description: The last recorded closing price for each selection strictly before the selected stored kickoff. Rows at or after that kickoff are omitted; conflicting stored kickoffs require storedCommenceTime. A stored kickoff does not establish actual kickoff. `commence_time` is the scheduled start; team sports often start a minute or two late, so a close's `recorded_at` can fall shortly after it and is still a pre-game price. The closing line is the single most valuable row in the archive. Same shape, plan and 2-years-or-everything split as `openers`, including the `403 PLAN_REQUIRED` for a fixture older than the plan covers.

closing.summary: The last price recorded before kickoff

get.summary: Recorded full-game prop checkpoints for one fixture
get.description: Full-game player prop checkpoints recorded from capture activation onward. Requires Scale or Business. Scale covers fixtures starting in the last 2 years. Use aggregate soccer or tennis keys; league and tournament selectors are rejected. Every player, stat, line and side is preserved. Openers are the first observation of each individual selection; closing prices must be observed before kickoff with a fresh source timestamp. No earlier prop prices are reconstructed. Coverage distinguishes recorded, observed_empty, failed and not_recorded. Halves and quarters are not archived.

200.description: Recorded full-game prop checkpoints for one fixture.

recorded.summary: Illustrative recorded prop checkpoints, not proof of fixture coverage

get.summary: Recorded full-game prop price changes for one fixture
get.description: Every recorded pre-match price change of every full-game player prop, from capture activation onward. Requires Scale or Business. Scale covers fixtures starting in the last 2 years. Same shape as the checkpoint series; each point is one change instant (checkpoint `move`) and carries every side's price at that instant plus whether the line was the book's main line. A price is recorded only when it changes, so an unchanged price between two points held. No earlier prices are reconstructed. Halves and quarters are not archived.

200.description: Recorded full-game prop price changes for one fixture.

recorded.summary: Illustrative recorded prop price changes, not proof of fixture coverage

Use aggregate soccer or tennis keys; league and tournament selectors are rejected. Every player, stat, line and side is preserved. get.summary: This key's plan, allowance and usage
get.description: Accepts an API key (unlike `/v1/account/keys`, which does not).

200.description: Usage for the presented key's account.

usage.summary: Mid-cycle usage on the Growth plan

get.summary: This account's plan, allowance and usage (signed-in session)
get.description: The same account-wide figure `/v1/account/usage` returns for a key: metering is per account, not per key. Signed-in website session only, like `/v1/account/keys`; an `X-API-Key` is refused here too. This is what the dashboard's "Usage" screen calls, since a key's plaintext is shown once at creation and never again, so there is no key on hand to send to the other operation.

usage.summary: Mid-cycle usage on the Growth plan

get.summary: Daily usage and per-key totals in this billing period
get.description: Signed-in website session only; API keys are refused. Returns one UTC calendar-day row for each day touched by the current billing period. A null request count means daily tracking did not yet cover that day, or the day is in the future; zero means tracking covered the day and no priced calls were charged. If tracking began during a day, that first day's count covers only the time after `coverage_start`. Per-key counts are whole-period totals from the existing monthly ledger, including revoked live keys. Test keys never spend the monthly allowance and report zero. This account read is free and uses the dedicated usage-read speed bucket.

200.description: Current-period daily coverage and key totals for the signed-in account.

get.summary: This account's plan, allowance, billing period and launch price
get.description: Signed-in website session only, like `/v1/account/keys`; an `X-API-Key` is refused. `price_cents` is the launch sticker price for the resolved plan (`null` for Free), not necessarily what this account is being billed today; for that, see `/v1/billing/subscription`.

free.summary: The Free plan has no price

get.summary: List this account's API keys
get.description: Signed-in website session only. An `X-API-Key` is refused here. A key can read its own usage through `/v1/account/usage`, but it can never list, create or revoke keys, so one leaked key cannot take over the rest.

200.description: This account's keys. Never includes the full secret.

keys.summary: Two key records, including one revoked key

post.description: Signed-in website session only. The full secret is returned exactly once, in this response. We do not store the plaintext and cannot show it again. Key prefixes are `ok_live_` for a normal key and `ok_test_` for a test key, always clearly marked as test context.

201.description: The new key, with its one-time secret.

delete.description: Signed-in website session only. Revoking a key is immediate and permanent: it never accepts another request. Revoking one key never disturbs any of the account's other keys. Revoking a key that is already revoked succeeds the same way; it does not return an error.

post.summary: Start a checkout for a paid plan
post.description: Signed-in website session only; an `X-API-Key` is refused, so a leaked key cannot spend the account's money. Returns an order and the values the card form on the account page needs to check the card and save it with Tranzila; it charges nothing. The first charge happens on our side once the card is saved. The buyer is bound to the signed-in account server-side, so the plan, interval and add-on are the only things the caller controls: a price, `customer_id` or return URL in the request body is ignored. Free needs no checkout. An account that already has a subscription is refused with `ALREADY_SUBSCRIBED`; use `/v1/billing/change`.

x-websocket-feed.summary: Prices pushed as they change. An add-on (+$99/mo) on Growth and Scale, included on Business and Enterprise; refused on Free and Starter.

authentication.method: X-API-Key header at the WebSocket handshake, identical to REST.
authentication.note: No query-string key is accepted, same as REST. A browser client that cannot set a custom header at handshake time may instead carry the key in the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol subprotocol list; ask support if you need this documented in more detail before relying on it.

x-websocket-feed.plan_rules: In-play fixtures are included from Growth up, which is also the floor for the feed itself. The feed carries game markets only; player-prop subscriptions are rejected with BAD_SUBSCRIPTION. Read props by polling. Refused with 403 PLAN_REQUIRED (the same envelope REST uses) as the handshake's own HTTP response, before the connection is accepted.

connection_limits.description: Concurrent connections per API key. These limits may change; the welcome message reports the headroom available to your key.

errors.BAD_MESSAGE: Send a text JSON object of at most 65536 characters; eight consecutive malformed frames close with 1008.
errors.BAD_SUBSCRIPTION: Invalid sport/filter/format fields or unsupported player-prop markets; correct and subscribe again.
errors.ODDS_UNAVAILABLE: No picture is built yet; retry the subscription.

heartbeat.description: A server `heartbeat` message every 5 seconds, plus the underlying WebSocket protocol's own ping/pong (dead connections are dropped at that layer, not by the application heartbeat).

resume.description: Every `picture` and `changes` message carries a `resume_token`. Send it back as `{"type": "resume", "token": "<token>"}` on a new connection to replay whatever changed while you were gone. If the gap was too long (or the token is unrecognised), the server answers `picture_required` instead of silently re-snapshotting -- send a fresh `subscribe`.

close_codes.1008: Eight consecutive malformed text/non-JSON/binary frames; correct the client.
close_codes.1013: Feed capacity is full; back off and retry.
close_codes.4001: Reserved for a future explicit post-accept auth failure.
close_codes.4002: Slow consumer: your outgoing queue on the server could not be drained in time. Reconnect and consider a narrower subscription.
close_codes.4003: Connection limit reached for this API key's plan. `connections_available` in the `welcome` message tells you how much headroom you have before opening another.

subscribe.description: Replaces this connection's subscription outright (a filter change is a new subscribe, not a separate message) and triggers a fresh `picture`.

markets.description: Defaults to h2h, spreads, totals, same as game-odds REST. Player-prop keys are not supported.

periods.description: Omitted means full game; full, all, 1h, 2h, 1q..4q, 1p..3p, f5, 1i, 1s..5s, reg as on polling.

confirmations.description: Grouped confirmations by default; legacy preserves individual unchanged entries for existing parsers. Resume tokens retain the selected format.

unsubscribe.description: Stops following anything; the connection idles (heartbeats only) until the next subscribe.

resume.description: Reconnect and replay missed changes, or get picture_required.

pong.description: Optional application-level acknowledgement of a heartbeat. Not required for liveness (the WebSocket protocol's own ping/pong is what matters).

welcome.description: The first message on every accepted connection.

picture.description: Everything the current subscription covers, sent whole. Each row is the SAME shape GET /v1/sports/{sport}/odds returns, so you can reuse your REST parser. Too big for one frame and it arrives as several consecutive `picture` frames instead -- see `part`/`parts` below.

changes.description: Only what changed since the last message for this subscription, grouped to at most one message per second. `upserts` and `removals` are both keyed by `scope` (fixture, bookmaker, market, outcome, or for upserts only `confirmed`, `unchanged` and `status`) at the coarsest level that actually changed -- a whole market pulled is ONE market-scoped removal, not one per outcome. A price is sent only when it moves. When a book re-confirms a market and no price in it moved, the feed batches confirmations sharing the exact bookmaker and timestamp into a `confirmed` entry (`bookmaker`, `last_update`, `markets`). Each item in `markets` names `event_id`, `market` and optional `period`; advance only those named markets, never every market of a fixture or bookmaker. Groups contain at most 256 targets. Set `confirmations: legacy` in every subscribe message to retain individual `unchanged` entries (`event_id`, `bookmaker`, `market`, optional `period`, `last_update`). Existing parsers must either support `confirmed` or request legacy. Prices remain exactly as last received with their exact confirmation clock; no timestamp is rounded or replaced. Resume tokens are bound to the format: changing format requires a fresh subscribe/picture. For a streaming book this can reflect proof of connection life rather than a new price message. An `outcome` upsert's `last_update` likewise advances its whole market. A bookmaker whose `link` changes is sent again whole, as one bookmaker-scoped upsert. A fixture's `is_live` flipping (kickoff, or the game passing its finish cut-off) is one compact `status` upsert (`event_id`, `is_live`); no prices are restated for it. Can split into several frames the same way `picture` can.

part_and_parts.description: Every `picture`/`changes` message carries `part` and `parts`. Normally both are 1. A message too big for one WebSocket frame (a busy sport's default `picture` can run several megabytes -- well past the 1 MiB default frame size of common client libraries) arrives instead as several consecutive frames of the same `type`, `part` 1..`parts` in order, never interleaved with another message and never split mid-fixture or mid-entry. Every part shares one `cursor`/`resume_token`; reassemble by concatenating `data` (or `upserts`/`removals`) across parts and treat the message complete once `part == parts`. Keep a `resume_token` only from a complete message (the frame where `part == parts`); if the connection drops between parts, discard the partial message and resume with the token of the last complete one.

picture_required.description: A resume could not be honoured; send a fresh subscribe.

error.description: A problem with a message on an already-open connection (not a handshake refusal, which uses the ordinary REST error envelope as the WebSocket's HTTP denial response instead). Same `code` vocabulary as REST's `error.code`.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description: Every operation except `/v1/account/keys` accepts this. There is no `?apiKey=` query fallback.

BearerAuth.description: A signed-in website session's access token. Required by `/v1/account/keys`. An `X-API-Key` is refused there: only a signed-in customer creates or revokes keys.

storedCommenceTimeQuery.name: storedCommenceTime
storedCommenceTimeQuery.description: Select an exact stored listed kickoff from error.stored_commence_times or historical discovery. ISO with timezone or Unix seconds. Required when multiple eligible stored kickoffs remain. Empty duplicate kickoffs are not choices when another kickoff has recorded prices; selecting one returns INVALID_STORED_COMMENCE_TIME. Entirely empty tracked fixtures remain selectable. No archival prices are rewritten.

sportPath.name: sport
sportPath.description: A sport key, for example `nfl`, `soccer`, `tennis`, `epl` or `tennis_atp_hangzhou`. `soccer` and `tennis` are aggregate keys with optional competition selectors; their legacy per-competition keys remain aliases. A well-formed tennis tournament key is accepted; one we carry no fixtures for this week returns an empty list.

historicalSportPath.name: sport
historicalSportPath.description: A historical sport key: `nfl`, `ncaaf`, `nba`, `wnba`, `mlb`, `nhl`, `mma`, aggregate `soccer` or aggregate `tennis`. `nhl` and `mlb` serve the same franchise fixtures as their live routes. A soccer league key such as `epl` serves only fixtures whose league was recorded when they were archived; older fixtures are served by the aggregate `soccer` key only. An event outside the key's league answers `404 UNKNOWN_EVENT`, like an unknown ID. League and tournament query selectors are rejected with `400 BAD_REQUEST`. Tournament-specific `tennis_*` keys are not supported by history.

eventIdPath.name: id
eventIdPath.description: A fixture id, as returned by `GET /v1/sports/{sport}/events`. Treat as opaque.

leagueQuery.name: league
leagueQuery.description: Optional soccer competition selector, using its existing public alias key (`epl`, not an internal provider slug). Only valid with the aggregate `soccer` sport key. Omitting it returns every currently available soccer competition in one response, which may be larger.

tournamentQuery.name: tournament
tournamentQuery.description: Optional tennis competition selector, without the legacy `tennis_` path prefix (`atp_beijing`, not `tennis_atp_beijing`). Only valid with aggregate `tennis`. Omitting it returns every currently available tennis competition in one response, which may be larger.

keyIdPath.name: keyId
keyIdPath.description: An API key's `id`, as returned by `GET /v1/account/keys`.

marketsQuery.name: markets
marketsQuery.description: Comma-separated market keys, with no period in them (`h2h`, `h2h_3_way`, `spreads`, `totals`, `team_totals`, ...); choose periods with `periods`. Omitting it returns the available main markets (`h2h,spreads,totals`). Requesting full-game `spreads`, `totals` or `team_totals` includes its main line followed by every available alternate line in that one market object (one object per team for `team_totals`). A period market has the same shape: one object per market key and period, holding every line the bookmaker posts, main line first. Outside soccer, a moneyline with a separately priced Draw uses `h2h_3_way`; two-way prices stay under `h2h`. Soccer keeps its standard result including Draw under `h2h`. NHL regulation-time results use `h2h_3_way` with `period: reg`. Request `markets=h2h,h2h_3_way` to receive both contracts, and select periods separately (for example `periods=1q`). Default markets remain `h2h,spreads,totals` and exclude `h2h_3_way`.

periodsQuery.name: periods
periodsQuery.description: Comma-separated periods for the requested `markets`: `1h`, `2h` (halves), `1q`..`4q` (quarters), `1p`..`3p` (hockey periods), `f5` (baseball first 5 innings), `1i` (baseball first inning), `1s`..`5s` (tennis sets), `reg` (hockey regulation time). Omitting it returns the full game only. `full` asks for the full game beside other periods (`periods=full,1h`); it is accepted here only, since a full-game market carries no `period`. `all` returns the full game and every period. An unknown period is `422 INVALID_MARKET`. There are no F3 or F7 markets.

propMarketsQuery.name: markets
propMarketsQuery.description: Comma-separated player-prop market keys, with no period in them, for example `player_pass_yds` or `player_anytime_td`; choose periods with `periods`. Required: there is no default set of props.

bookmakersQuery.name: bookmakers
bookmakersQuery.description: Comma-separated, case-sensitive book keys from `/v1/bookmakers`. A typo or wrong case returns `422 INVALID_BOOKMAKER` with a suggested key and `valid_bookmakers`; it does not count against your allowance. Defaults to every book when omitted. On the odds and props routes, any book you name that returns no markets for a fixture is listed in that fixture's `unmatched_bookmakers`.

dateFormatQuery.name: dateFormat
dateFormatQuery.description: How `commence_time`, every `last_update` and `recorded_at`, and `archive_from` are written: ISO-8601 UTC strings with exactly three fractional digits and trailing Z (`iso`, e.g. `2026-10-11T13:00:00.000Z`) or unix seconds (`unix`). ISO sub-millisecond digits are truncated. Unix price clocks may be fractional; fixture and gameline archive times use whole seconds.

eventIdsQuery.name: eventIds
eventIdsQuery.description: Comma-separated fixture ids, to narrow a list call to specific fixtures.

commenceTimeFromQuery.name: commenceTimeFrom
commenceTimeFromQuery.description: Only fixtures commencing at or after this ISO-8601 UTC instant.

commenceTimeToQuery.name: commenceTimeTo
commenceTimeToQuery.description: Only fixtures commencing at or before this ISO-8601 UTC instant.

tryItPathQuery.name: path
tryItPathQuery.description: Encoded public read path and optional query string to run.

x-requests-last.description: What this one call cost against the allowance (0 for a free call).

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: This plan's speed limit, in requests per second.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current one-second window.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until the speed-limit window resets.

X-Request-Id.description: This request's id, for support and for matching against `error.request_id`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying on 429 SPEED_LIMIT or 503 ODDS_UNAVAILABLE.

coverage_start.description: Earliest instant from which daily counts are complete. If the existing monthly total was zero when daily tracking began, this is the period start (or the tracking instant if a concurrently healed anchor is briefly in the future); otherwise it is the instant tracking began. During a rolling API release, a monthly write from an older worker without a daily write advances coverage to the detection instant and discards that day's incomplete bar. The containing UTC day can be partial. A call accepted just before a concurrently healed anchor is attributed to the first UTC day of its new billing period.

requests.description: Successful priced calls, or null outside known coverage.

by_key.description: Keys owned by this account, including revoked keys; newest first.

requests.description: Whole-period charged calls for this key; always zero for test keys.

kind.description: `sportsbook`, `exchange` or `prediction_market` today; new kinds may appear.

markets.description: The main rung only, keyed h2h / spreads / totals; a key absent means the book has none.

PublicFeaturedCard.description: One homepage card. `columns` are the sides in display order: away then home, or for soccer home, Draw, away. Each row's `prices` and `best` follow that order.

website.description: Leave blank. This field exists to detect automated submissions.

key.description: The sport key: one league or one tennis tournament.

active.description: Whether this league/tournament is in season right now.

has_outrights.description: Always `false` in v1. Outright and futures markets are not served yet.

kind.description: `sportsbook`, `exchange` or `prediction_market` today. More kinds may be added.

sports.description: Sport keys we have observed this book pricing, at the coarse group level (`nfl`, `soccer`, `tennis`, ...) rather than a per-league breakdown for soccer. This is what we have measured, not a schedule: a sport currently out of season can be missing here even though the book carries it, until it is observed pricing that sport again. Its absence is not a claim the book will never carry it.

has_player_props.description: Whether this book has a player-props integration at all, not in every sport.

player_props_sports.description: Source-verified sport groups supported by this integration when known. Omitted where a sport-specific capability has not been verified. BetUS supports MLB/NHL, Circa MLB, SBOBET WNBA, SportBet NBA/WNBA, and Shuffle NFL/NCAAF/MLB/NHL/NBA/WNBA. Omission is not an empty capability list. For bet365 this is `nfl` and `nhl`. NFL coverage currently includes full-game N+ passing, rushing and receiving ladders plus first, last, anytime and multiple-touchdown selections. It does not promise Under, period or in-play props. Availability still depends on the fixture and current source prices.

size_kind.description: What a `size` from this book means, matching `outcomes[].size.kind` (see `Size` below). `null` when this book has never been seen publishing a size.

key.description: The market key exactly as it appears in `markets[].key` (or a prop row's `stat`), and the value `markets` takes.

has_point.description: Whether this market's outcomes carry a `point` (a spread, a total line, or a player prop's line). False for a fixed choice among outcomes (moneyline, both-teams-to-score, draw-no-bet, double chance) and for a player prop that is simply true or false (anytime touchdown scorer, double-double).

kind.description: `game_line` or `player_prop`. Treat the list as open: a new kind may be added. `game_line` is a market on the fixture, served by `/v1/sports/{sport}/odds`. `player_prop` is a market on one named player, served by `/v1/sports/{sport}/props`, where `markets` is required.

sports.description: Sport tags this market applies to. Coarse (`nfl`, `soccer`, `tennis`), not the per-league `/v1/sports` keys.

bookmakers.description: Book keys known to carry this market: measured game-line coverage or source-backed player-prop mappings within supported sports. Describes capability, not current availability on a fixture. Omitted where coverage is unverified, including period props without an explicit mapping. Never assumes every props book carries every prop market.

id.description: A readable, constructible fixture id. Treat as opaque.

is_live.description: `true` from scheduled `commence_time` until the sport-specific live-window cutoff; `false` outside that window. Inferred from time, not a confirmed match-status or final-result feed, except reliable source terminal evidence makes it false. See the additive status and status_evidence fields. A delayed start, early finish or unusually long fixture can disagree with this flag. Evaluated when the response is served, so it can flip without a price change. On the WebSocket feed a flip arrives as a `status` upsert. Historical routes apply the same time-derived rule.

status.description: On current fixture routes, scheduled means the fixture has not started, including a delayed start. Live requires is_live to be true and a fresh observation of a linked book's own in-play state, identified by status_evidence. Unknown means neither live play nor finish is confirmed. Finished requires retained explicit terminal evidence. These values are additive; clients must accept new values. Historical props use their separately documented recording status. Archive presence and absent prices alone never prove finish.

score.description: Present only for covered live soccer and tennis fixtures with a fresh observation. All sides follow home_team and away_team. Soccer clocks are cumulative observed match time, without extrapolation. Tennis totals count completed sets; ambiguous totals are omitted. Uncovered or stale scores are absent.

status_evidence.description: The book, its observed state and observation time supporting live or finished status. Absent when no supporting observation is available.

League.description: Soccer fixtures only: the league a fixture belongs to. `key` is the public sport key when the league has one (`epl`; pass it as `soccer?league=` or as the sport key), else a stable key for that league; `title` is its display name. `null` when the league is not known for the fixture. Historical bodies carry the same object; a fixture archived before its league was recorded has `league: null` unless the sport key you asked with names one (`epl`). Other sports carry no `league` (tennis carries `tournament`; every other sport key is one league).

Tournament.description: Tennis fixtures only: the tournament a match belongs to. `key` is the tournament's public sport key (`tennis_atp_hangzhou`; pass it as `tennis?tournament=` or as the sport key); `title` is its display name. `null` when the tournament is not known. Historical bodies carry the same object.

Timestamp.description: An instant. ISO-8601 UTC (`2026-09-20T17:00:00.000Z`) by default, integer unix seconds under `dateFormat=unix`.

IsoTimestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC with exactly three fractional digits and a trailing `Z`.

PriceTimestamp.description: When the book confirmed a price. ISO-8601 UTC with exactly three fractional digits and trailing Z, or seconds since the epoch under `dateFormat=unix`, optionally fractional.

PriceUnixTimestamp.description: Seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z, optionally fractional for measured prices.

Price.description: One number per price. An integer under the default `oddsFormat=american`, a decimal number above 1 under `oddsFormat=decimal`.

AmericanPrice.description: American odds: an integer of +100 or more, or -100 or less (`124`, `-110`). Never between -100 and +100, and never fractional.

DecimalPrice.description: Decimal odds, the total return per unit staked, stake included (`1.91`).

kind.description: `posted_limit`: one number that applies to both legs, a sportsbook's maximum bet. `resting_depth`: a separate number per leg, an exchange's live order book. `contracts`: a contract count; no bookmaker uses it today (Kalshi and Polymarket report `resting_depth` in dollars at the best price). More kinds may be added. The kind is fixed per bookmaker (`GET /v1/bookmakers` `size_kind`).

amount.description: Always a positive number. A `posted_limit` or `resting_depth` amount is in the bookmaker's own currency; a `contracts` amount is a count. The same object appears on every line the bookmaker states a size for, including alternate lines and periods.

name.description: The team, player or side this price is for. Never `home`/`away`. On `h2h`, `h2h_3_way` and `spreads` a team outcome is named exactly as the fixture's `away_team` or `home_team`, and outcomes are listed away team first, then home team, then `Draw` on a three-way moneyline. Totals are `Over` then `Under`.

description.description: Present where `name` alone does not say what the price is for. On `team_totals` (and its period variants) `name` is `Over` or `Under` and `description` is the team the total belongs to.

point.description: The line/spread/total this price is for, always written as a decimal number (`2.5`, `-3.0`). Absent (not present) on h2h and h2h_3_way.

main.description: Present on every spread, total and team-total ladder outcome, including periods and opening/closing history; omitted on partial series points. True on the main line, false on alternates. The main line comes first: the book's featured two-sided line when named, otherwise the most balanced two-sided line by implied probability. A one-sided line is main only when no two-sided line exists. Lines with an implied probability sum at or below 1.25 take priority over lines above 1.25. Extreme prices are kept as quoted.

Period.description: The slice of the game a market settles on: `1h`/`2h` halves, `1q`..`4q` quarters, `1p`..`3p` hockey periods, `f5` baseball's first 5 innings, `1i` baseball's first inning, `1s`..`5s` tennis sets, `reg` hockey regulation time. Absent on a full-game market; never `full`. More periods may be added. There are no F3 or F7 markets.

key.description: Market key, with no period in it (`spreads`). Outside soccer, three-way moneylines use `h2h_3_way`, including NHL `period: reg`; two-way prices use `h2h`. Soccer results including Draw keep `h2h`. Full-game `spreads`, `totals` and `team_totals` (one object per team) each contain their main line first followed by available alternate lines.

last_update.description: This market's measured confirmation time: when several rungs are combined, the oldest included rung confirmation. Outcomes do not carry separate clocks. ISO-8601 UTC, unix seconds under `dateFormat=unix`, or `null` when it is not measured. ISO timestamps carry exactly three fractional digits (for example, `2026-09-29T07:50:29.043Z`) and the Z suffix; sub-millisecond digits are truncated.

BookmakerLink.description: A link to this fixture on the bookmaker's own website. Present only when the bookmaker gives one; the field is absent otherwise, never empty or `null`. Some bookmakers link to the competition page rather than the single event. This is an event-page link; it does not select an outcome or populate a bet slip.

last_update.description: This book's own last-confirmed time for this fixture, never earlier than any of its markets' `last_update`. `null` if unmeasured. For a streaming book, this is the later of its last price message and its last proof of connection life.

unmatched_bookmakers.description: Sorted book keys the response could not serve for this fixture. With `bookmakers=`, every book you asked for that returned no markets here (not listed, not matched to the fixture safely, none of the markets you asked for, or too old to serve). Without `bookmakers=`, a book that reached us with a price for this fixture that we could not serve (not matched to it safely, or too old to serve); a book that does not list the fixture at all is not named. Present, and possibly empty, on every successful response.

PropOutcome.description: One side of a prop line. `price` is absent only on a pick'em book (`prizepicks`), which posts a line and the sides you may pick (More/Less, served as `Over`/`Under`, or `Yes` on a line-less prop) and never a price. Every other book always carries `price`.

name.description: `Over`, `Under`, `Yes` or `No` today. More sides may be added.

player.description: The player's name, spelled the same way on every row of the fixture whatever the book calls them. A team defense is a player too, for example "SEA D/ST".

player_id.description: A fixed id for the player, the same on every book and every day: join on it, not on the name. Never changed once served.

stat.description: A player-prop market key, with no period in it, for example player_pass_yds.

point.description: The line for this stat. Absent for a binary (Yes/No) prop.

main.description: True on exactly one row per bookmaker, player and stat: that book's main line, which comes first among its lines. It is the line priced on both sides with the most even prices; a line priced on one side only (a milestone such as "250+ yards") is main only when the book prices no line on both sides. A Yes/No prop is always main. On a pick'em book, which posts no prices, the main line is the book's standard line; its other lines for that player and stat are alternates.

unmatched_bookmakers.description: Sorted book keys with no returned props for this fixture and the selected markets. With `bookmakers=`, covers the named books; without it, covers all props-capable catalogue books. Does not diagnose the reason for absence.

main.description: Movement points only. Whether this line was the book's main line for the player and stat at that instant.

stat.description: A player-prop market key, with no period in it, for example player_pass_yds.

point.description: The line for this stat. Absent for a binary (Yes/No) prop.

stat.description: A player-prop market key, with no period in it, for example player_pass_yds.

point.description: The line for this stat. Absent for a binary (Yes/No) prop.

HistoricalOutcome.description: A recorded sportsbook price or exchange/prediction-market probability quote. Probability quotes use the existing bookmaker key (polymarket, kalshi, sxbet, shuffle or sportbet). Their price is null in either odds format; bid_prob, ask_prob and mid_prob are present, with null for any missing value. No complementary side or American/decimal price is inferred. Venue checkpoints have no opening line. Size is not recorded for these quotes.

mid_prob.description: Mean of bid and ask when both exist, otherwise null.

status.description: `recorded` or `not_recorded` today. More values may be added.

recorded_at.description: The oldest capture time among the outcomes included in this market's checkpoint. Outcomes may have been captured at different times. `null` when `status` is `not_recorded`.

outcomes.description: Team names match the fixture's display names. Moneyline outcomes are away, home, then Draw; spreads are away then home per mirrored rung. Totals are Over then Under per rung.

ArchiveFrom.description: Earliest available archive filename month-start, not the first quote or capture date. Null if no archive files exist.

history_status.description: Fixture-level recording result; recorded_no_rows means a stored fixture has no returned price rows; it makes no claim about price movement.

coverage_note.description: Explanation of the stored history result.

id.description: ID accepted by historical price routes.

home_team.description: Team display name using the same normalization as current odds.

away_team.description: Team display name using the same normalization as current odds.

status.description: Stored metadata exists; does not establish actual match completion.

score.description: The recorded final score, the same object as the current routes' `score`. All sides follow home_team and away_team. Absent when the archive holds no final score.

SeriesPoint.description: When change rows exist, the first point for each bookmaker and market contains the full market; later points contain only changed outcomes (price, point or size), each with its own values, plus recorded_at. Apply points in order to rebuild the market. A since-bounded request starts with a full market at the first emitted time, seeded from earlier changes. Without change rows, every checkpoint point contains the whole recorded market.

outcomes.description: Same display names and away/home per-rung ordering as current odds and historical checkpoints.

size.description: Recorded size on change-series outcomes; null when unknown.

movement.description: `recorded`: more than one recorded timestamp group. `no_movement`: exactly one recorded timestamp group; this does not prove prices stayed unchanged between checkpoints. `not_recorded`: nothing in the archive for this market on this fixture, either from before the archive began or never captured. More values may be added.

plan.description: `free`, `starter`, `growth`, `scale`, `business` or `enterprise` today. A plan may be added.

requests_allowance.description: This plan's monthly request allowance, or `null` for `enterprise` (its volume is whatever the contract says; it is never refused for volume).

requests_last_second.description: Requests this account made in the last completed second that counted against its speed limit. Calls to `/v1/account/usage/session` are not included.

requests_allowance.description: This plan's monthly request allowance, or `null` for `enterprise` (its volume is whatever the contract says; it is never refused for volume).

price_cents.description: The plan's launch sticker price in cents, `{month, year}`. `null` for the free plan (no price) and for `enterprise` (sold by contract, "from $499" is not a checkout price). This is the LIST price for the plan, not necessarily what this account is being billed (see `/v1/billing/subscription`).

prefix.description: The key's non-secret prefix, safe to display, for example `ok_live_REDACTED`: the key's own leading `ok_live_` or `ok_test_`, plus its first 8 characters.

last_four.description: The key's last 4 characters, safe to display alongside the prefix so you can tell two of your keys apart even when their prefixes match.

test.description: True for a key created with `test: true`, always clearly marked as test context.
Create an `ok_test_`-prefixed key instead of a live one.

key.description: The full secret. Returned only here, only once. We do not store the plaintext.

Subscription.description: An account's subscription. The card is described only by its last four digits.

plan.description: A plan slug, for example `api_growth`. New plans may be added.

addon.description: Whether the live-feed add-on is included.

status.description: `active`, or `past_due` when the last renewal failed and the card must be updated.

pending_change.description: A change that takes effect at the next renewal.

amount_cents.description: What one renewal charges, in cents.

stored_commence_times.description: Stored Unix-second choices on AMBIGUOUS_EVENT or INVALID_STORED_COMMENCE_TIME; independent of dateFormat.

valid_bookmakers.description: Valid case-sensitive book keys on INVALID_BOOKMAKER.

current_plan.description: 403 only: the plan on the presented key.

required_plan.description: 403 only: the lowest plan that includes this request. For history, that depends on how long ago the fixture started as well as on the endpoint.
